---
title: "Cases"
subtitle: "Four molecules, carried through everything"
---

Every case is **fictional** and **simulated from a documented generative
model**. Nothing here derives from a real programme, a company dataset, or any
patient. The true parameters are published alongside the data.

That is not a compromise forced by data access — it is a pedagogical advantage.
When you fit a model to these data you can compare your estimate to the value
that generated it, which is the one experiment a real dataset can never offer.

## CASE-SM · "Ozanib" {#case-sm}

Oral small molecule, CYP3A4 substrate, once daily for 21 days.

| | |
|---|---|
| Structure | Two-compartment, first-order absorption, linear elimination |
| Design | 60 subjects, 25 / 50 / 100 mg once daily; rich sampling on days 1 and 14, troughs on days 7, 10, 21 |
| True typical values | $CL/F$ 12 L/h · $V_c/F$ 60 L · $Q/F$ 8 L/h · $V_p/F$ 90 L · $k_a$ 1.2 h⁻¹ |
| Real covariate effects | Allometric weight (0.75 on clearances, 1.0 on volumes); strong CYP3A4 inhibitor multiplies $CL/F$ by 0.45 |
| Deliberate decoys | `CRCL`, `AGE`, `SEX` and `ALT` are recorded and have **no** true effect |
| Variability | IIV 30% on $CL$, 25% on $V_c$, 45% on $k_a$, correlated $CL$–$V_c$; combined 20% proportional + 0.5 ng/mL additive residual |
| Censoring | LLOQ 1 ng/mL; ~4% of samples BLQ, flagged and set to `NA` |
| Files | `cases/case-sm/` — `generate.py`, `generate.R`, `truth.yml`, `data/` |

### Three deliberate traps

- **Everything is apparent (`/F`).** There is no IV arm, so bioavailability is
  not identifiable. Reporting "clearance is 12 L/h" is a real error, and the
  case is built to expose it.
- **Four covariates do nothing.** They exist so covariate-selection lessons have
  genuine false positives to catch. Please do not "fix" this.
- **A corrupted copy exists.** `ozanib_pk_messy.csv` carries eleven injected
  data-assembly defects with a manifest, used in
  [S0-03](lessons/s0-03-data-assembly/index.qmd).

### Reproducing it

```bash
python cases/case-sm/generate.py        # the clean dataset
python cases/case-sm/make_messy.py      # the corrupted copy plus its manifest
```

The generator was validated against an independent implementation, and against
the analytical two-compartment solution, before the data shipped. For any linear
model $AUC_{\tau,ss} = D/CL$ exactly — at 50 mg that is 4166.7 ng·h/mL, and the
simulation reproduces it to four figures.

## When you outgrow synthetic data

The cases here are simulated so that your answer can be graded against a
published truth. That is their whole reason for existing, and it is also their
limit: nothing in `CASE-SM` will surprise you in the way real data does, because
nothing in it is accidental.

When you are ready for data that nobody arranged for your benefit, these are
free and open (details on [Resources](resources.qmd)):

- [PK-DB](https://pk-db.com/) — 819 curated published studies, 17,285
  individuals, 6,103 concentration timecourses, open API, no registration.
- [`nlmixr2data`](https://nlmixr2.github.io/nlmixr2data/reference/index.html) —
  26 classic datasets including `Theoph`, warfarin and phenobarbital, plus
  `nmtest`, which carries reference NONMEM output to check a solver against.
- [Open Systems Pharmacology PBPK model library](https://github.com/Open-Systems-Pharmacology/OSP-PBPK-Model-Library)
  — around 45 published, qualified PBPK models for real drugs, runnable in the
  free PK-Sim suite.
- [DDMoRe Model Repository](https://repository.ddmore.foundation/) — 128
  published pharmacometric models with their original control streams. **Dormant
  since 2018**, so treat it as an archive rather than a living project, but it
  is still the largest free collection of NONMEM-style models.
- [BioModels](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/biomodels/) — 3,595 systems-biology models
  in SBML, 1,096 of them manually curated. The starting point for `S4`.
